body:
I've been working on a proof-of-concept that addresses this. PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/117452

The PoC adds automatic script discovery for referenced assemblies (<ProjectReference> and <PackageReference>), so [Export], [GlobalClass], and lifecycle methods (_Ready, _Process, etc.) work for scripts defined in external projects.

The recommended layout places project.godot at the solution root, with the main .csproj and module projects as subdirectories — all source files stay under res:// with full editor integration. A new dotnet/project/project_directory setting supports .csproj in a subdirectory.

Working example project with 3 assembly types (in-tree ProjectReference, Godot SDK ProjectReference, NuGet PackageReference): https://github.com/matelq/GodotMultiAssemblyReference

This is a PoC and request for feedback, not a final implementation. Maintainer input on the approach is welcome.
